title: Block Core
summary: One building cannot lift up a neighborhood, but a series of smaller interventions tuned to the specific needs of a block can better address what the built environment is lacking.
body: Block Core takes a single corner in Kensington and asks what the smallest version of the idea looks like — enough program to be useful on its own, small enough to be built without waiting for anything else.

The zoning allows 62 feet across 80% of the site; this stops at 40, keeping the corner in scale with the rowhouses either side. A restaurant and community kitchen occupy the ground floor, sharing one long table and an open range, with long-term residences on the two floors above. The two occupancies are separated as the code requires without being separated as experience: the residents' front door is part of the same corner as the kitchen's.
The construction is drawn as carefully as the plan — triple-glazed windows to the south, cellulose insulation, magnesium oxide sheathing, timber beams sitting on recycled concrete.
